proposals.title: Seven-layer causal navigator
proposals.bookReference: Pinned Proving Nothing, Chapter 1, 'The Seven Layers at a Glance' (B07 lines 272-298); Chapter 10, 'The Causal Web: Why It Is a DAG, Not a Stack' (B07 lines 4460-4479); exact supplied excerpts in B08-EXACT-MANUSCRIPT-SECTIONS.json.
proposals.sourceSupport: The book names seven concerns and says their dependencies do not follow the numbering. It describes cross-layer design pressures, a DAG, and a coupled 4-5-6 proof core. It also distinguishes design-time constraints from runtime transaction flow.
proposals.websiteMapping: Add a navigator to the existing Webs explainer. Map the book's concerns to questions readers can ask about a Moriarty financial transition, and link back to Webs, Strands, statements, proofs, and the consuming contract. These links are explanatory product mappings, not evidence that Moriarty implements a ZK stack matching each node.
proposals.readerCopy: A proof system is shaped by connected choices. Choose a layer to see what question it answers and how that question relates to a financial transition.
proposals.interaction: Seven keyboard-selectable nodes open a detail panel. Selecting a node highlights only documented, labeled connections and displays related layers as text. Include an always-visible legend distinguishing book description, Webs mapping, and implementation status.
proposals.diagram: A labeled directed dependency map, not a seven-step rail. Visually cluster Layers 4, 5, and 6 as the proof core. Include at least the source's Layer 7-to-5/6, Layer 4-to-2, and Layer 3/4 fusion examples. Label this a conceptual book map, and keep runtime transaction flow in a separate view.
questions: Which exact Chapter 10 edges and labels will the security/editorial owner approve for publication?
Which Webs concepts are adopted copy versus explanatory mapping, and which are still unknown?
proposals.limits: The book calls its dependency model a DAG while also describing bidirectional pressures. Do not claim the website resolves that distinction or independently validates every edge. The seven nodes do not establish proof coverage, security, or implementation support.

proposals.title: Always-findable setup and Groth16 facts
proposals.bookReference: Pinned Proving Nothing, Chapter 2, 'Universal versus Circuit-Specific Setups' (B07 lines 609-621; B05); setup participant statement in Chapter 1, 'The Seven Layers at a Glance' (B07 lines 272-298). Groth16 concept reference B06.
proposals.sourceSupport: The supplied book text says Groth16 proofs in the cited construction are 192 bytes and its setup is circuit-specific. It separately names 141,416 participants in the Ethereum KZG Summoning of 2023. These facts refer to different setups and must not be merged.
proposals.websiteMapping: Put a setup facts card inside the navigator and link it from the existing Implementation navigation. Add a technical-status appendix with explicit unknown values where the supplied product evidence gives no current inventory/count.
proposals.readerCopy: Groth16: 192 bytes in the cited construction; setup is circuit-specific. Ethereum KZG Summoning (2023): 141,416 participants. These describe different systems. Moriarty setup and circuit counts are not established by this page's source packet.
proposals.interaction: Expose a persistent 'Setup & proof size' link. Expand the setup card in place; provide source citations next to each number and a separate 'Moriarty implementation status' link to the appendix.
proposals.diagram: Two clearly separated fact blocks—Groth16 and Ethereum KZG ceremony—with distinct labels, units, and source references. No combined counter, inferred total, or product status badge.
questions: Can the book's cited Groth16 size statement be retained verbatim after the assigned cryptographic fact-check?
Is there an approved, current source for Moriarty setup counts, circuit inventory, or supported proof APIs?
proposals.limits: This is a visual placement proposal, not independent cryptographic verification. Do not imply the KZG participant count is a Groth16 count or either is a Moriarty count. The current product counts remain unknown in the inputs read.

proposals.title: Connect the seven-layer explainer to the invoice anchor
proposals.bookReference: Pinned Proving Nothing, Chapter 1 layer descriptions (B07 lines 272-298); Chapter 10 runtime/design distinction (B07 lines 4460-4479). Product anchor observed in supplied qa-v2-intermediate/explorer.png and desktop-top.png.
proposals.sourceSupport: The book presents the layers as a way to reason about proof systems and distinguishes design-time dependencies from runtime flow. The supplied Webs explorer shows staged invoice escrow, a payment amount control, required roles for payment arithmetic, fee accounting, and duty continuation, plus statement/context details.
proposals.websiteMapping: Preserve staged invoice escrow as the default concrete case and the existing Explore/Follow-the-value navigation. Let a reader open a role, see the statement/context, then follow an explanatory link to relevant layer concepts and return to the same invoice state.
proposals.readerCopy: Start with the transition: the invoice example shows the required proof roles. The layer map explains connected design choices behind proof systems; it does not replace the transition's required roles.
proposals.interaction: Keep the amount-change control and required-role selection available. Add contextual 'How this relates to the proof layers' links that open the navigator without losing the chosen amount or selected role. Retain a clear route back to the invoice example.
proposals.diagram: Two adjacent but distinct visuals: the current required-role Web and the book's layer-dependency map. A labeled connector may show 'product example' to 'background concept'; do not draw a direct one-to-one line from each role to one layer.
questions: Does the existing invoice amount/CTA remain the primary first interaction in the adopted page copy?
Which exact role-to-layer contextual links does the product owner want to present, if any?
proposals.limits: Screenshot inspection does not establish runtime behavior or acceptance. No role-to-layer equivalence is evidenced. Preserve the Webs distinction between computed proof roles and authenticated transaction premises as stated in the supplied explorer.

proposals.title: Five financial-case selector with layer context
proposals.bookReference: Pinned Proving Nothing, Chapter 10 causal examples and layer interactions (B07 lines 4460-4479). Five case labels observed in supplied qa-v2-intermediate/explorer.png.
proposals.sourceSupport: The existing explorer screenshot names Staged invoice escrow, Batched DEX orders, Capped issuance, Loan servicing, and Treasury allocation. The book says design pressures vary across proof architectures. The supplied materials do not establish a verified seven-layer implementation map for any of the five cases.
proposals.websiteMapping: Retain the five-case selector. Allow a user to switch the financial example and separately select a layer for general explanation. Populate per-case links only when adopted product copy supplies and verifies them.
proposals.readerCopy: Explore five financial examples. The layer navigator describes proof-system design questions; case-specific implementation details appear only where documented.
proposals.interaction: Keep the current scenario tabs. Selecting a case updates its existing role/statement detail; selecting a layer opens generic book-derived context. Show an explicit 'No case-specific mapping supplied' state rather than guessed layer assignments.
proposals.diagram: Scenario strip above the invoice/explorer details; layer map is a separate component with its own selection. Avoid a seven-by-five matrix that implies unsupported coverage.
questions: Are the five screenshot labels the final public case names?
Which scenario-to-layer mappings have approved source evidence?
proposals.limits: The screenshot is a visual artifact, not implementation evidence. Do not claim that any case exercises every layer or is verified by a particular layer.

proposals.title: Accessible responsive graph and reduced-motion mode
proposals.bookReference: Pinned Proving Nothing, Chapter 1 says the layer ordering is explanatory and interdependent (B07 lines 272-298); Chapter 10 supplies the dependency-web framing (B07 lines 4460-4479).
proposals.sourceSupport: The source structure contains seven named layers and directed/cross-layer examples. The interaction and accessibility behavior here are design recommendations, not claims from the book or current product behavior.
proposals.websiteMapping: Adapt the navigator to the supplied desktop and narrow-screen Webs layouts while preserving access to the invoice case, navigation, layer labels, and status appendix.
proposals.readerCopy: Choose a layer or follow a labeled connection. Every relationship is also available in text.
proposals.interaction: Use at least 44 CSS-pixel touch targets for graph controls and case selectors; keyboard-operable selection and visible focus; no horizontal scrolling at mobile widths; an equivalent text list; honor prefers-reduced-motion and avoid essential animated tracing.
proposals.diagram: Desktop: labeled map and detail panel. Mobile: simplified responsive SVG or stacked list with a Related Layers disclosure. Preserve edge direction and proof-core grouping; do not rely on hover, color alone, or animation.
questions: Which supported viewport widths and accessibility checks are part of the website's existing review process?
proposals.limits: These are proposed interaction requirements. The supplied screenshots show previews only; no browser, assistive-technology, or responsive tests were run.
